article_title: Solving instructional design dilemmas to develop a Video Enhanced Rubric with modeling examples to support mental model development of complex skills: the Viewbrics-project use case
citation: Kevin Ackermans, Ellen Rusman, Saskia Brand-Gruwel, Marcus Specht. (2019). Solving instructional design dilemmas to develop a Video Enhanced Rubric with modeling examples to support mental model development of complex skills: the Viewbrics-project use case. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-019-09668-1
title: Four-step Roles-Functions-Methods-Guidelines framework for prioritizing and selecting among conflicting design guidelines
description: The article introduces a step-by-step framework to address dilemmas between contradicting design guidelines when fostering complex skill development with multimedia. Designers "propose four steps to prioritize the methodological guidelines over the multimedia guidelines": first identify the role(s) of the artifact, second identify and rank its function(s) per role, third identify the method(s) needed to implement those functions given the target audience, and fourth derive the guideline(s) from the chosen methods in order of importance. Applied to the Viewbrics VER, this yielded two designs: an orientation role prioritizing motivation, and a Preparation, Evaluation and Selection role prioritizing feedback. The authors expect the approach to decrease design tensions for researchers and practitioners.
requirements: The artifact's roles, functions and methods must be identified and prioritized from top to bottom in order of importance before guidelines are selected
constraints: The framework was illustrated with a single use case (the Viewbrics VER in Dutch pre-university education)
target_learners: Educational researchers and practitioners designing multimedia for complex skill development
target_learning_goals: Design of technology-enhanced formative assessment supporting complex skill mastery
examples: In the Viewbrics use case, role 1 (orientation) prioritized motivation via ARCS, while role 2 (Preparation, Evaluation and Selection) prioritized feedback via the FA cycle and 4C/ID
key_sources: Kevin Ackermans, Ellen Rusman, Saskia Brand-Gruwel, Marcus Specht. (2019). Solving instructional design dilemmas to develop a Video Enhanced Rubric with modeling examples to support mental model development of complex skills: the Viewbrics-project use case. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-019-09668-1

article_title: Research on the student-centered research feedback experimental teaching model to enhance the effectiveness of pharmacology experimental teaching.
citation: Miao C, Chen J, Li Y, Xia A, Song Y, Xu C, Mao Y, Wang X. (2026). Research on the student-centered research feedback experimental teaching model to enhance the effectiveness of pharmacology experimental teaching. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000051199
title: Research feedback pharmacology experimental teaching model (RFPETM)
description: RFPETM is a student-centered pharmacology experimental teaching model that feeds the college's scientific research achievements into undergraduate teaching. It "included 10 experimental teaching projects, all of which came from the research achievements of our college," each lasting 4 teaching hours. Students work in self-selected groups of four, learn from self-built online resources and virtual simulation projects, independently search literature and design experimental routes, obtain teacher review of plans, then collect data, analyze statistics, and write reports. The model aims to exercise scientific research thinking and cultivate experimental operation, research thinking, and comprehensive practical abilities.
requirements: Teaching project library based on the pharmacology experimental teaching syllabus and institutional research achievements
Supervising teachers to review experimental plans and score classroom performance
Online and virtual simulation resources for pre-class learning
constraints: Studied at a single Chinese medical university with integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine majors; retains a proportion of confirmatory and comprehensive experiments
examples: Teaching projects included organophosphorus poisoning and rescue, effects of drugs on carotid blood pressure, and determination of the median lethal dose of dichlorvos and procaine
key_sources: Miao C, Chen J, Li Y, Xia A, Song Y, Xu C, Mao Y, Wang X. (2026). Research on the student-centered research feedback experimental teaching model to enhance the effectiveness of pharmacology experimental teaching. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000051199

article_title: Construction of research feedback experimental teaching mode for medical undergraduate students and comparative study with traditional experimental teaching mode.
citation: Miao Chenggui, Huang Yurong, Duan Qiangjun, Mao Yanmei, Chen Jiaqing, Li Yanping, Xia Aixin, Song Yinqiu, Wang Bing. (2025). Construction of research feedback experimental teaching mode for medical undergraduate students and comparative study with traditional experimental teaching mode. BMC Medical Education 25:961. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07538-4
title: Research feedback experimental teaching model (RFETM): a five-component reform of basic medical experimental teaching
description: The research feedback experimental teaching model (RFETM) is a reform of basic medical experimental teaching built 'from five aspects: RFETM teaching syllabus, teaching projects, teaching assessment, teaching conditions, and textbooks'. Its project library 'included 10 teaching projects and a total of 32 class hours', the first eight mandatory and the last two optional, supported by a virtual simulation platform for pre-class self-study and a newly compiled innovation experimental textbook.
requirements: Experimental teaching projects derived from the institution's scientific research achievements, with corresponding experimental conditions to ensure implementation of the teaching projects
constraints: Aimed at medical undergraduate students with a certain theoretical and experimental skills foundation
examples: The RFETM project library included projects such as preparation of an Alzheimer's disease rat model, acupuncture effects on gastric function in rats, RT-qPCR and Western blot detection, each mandatory project allocated 4 class hours.
key_sources: Miao Chenggui, Huang Yurong, Duan Qiangjun, Mao Yanmei, Chen Jiaqing, Li Yanping, Xia Aixin, Song Yinqiu, Wang Bing. (2025). Construction of research feedback experimental teaching mode for medical undergraduate students and comparative study with traditional experimental teaching mode. title: Virtual simulation experimental teaching platform for pre-class self-study of research techniques
description: A virtual simulation experimental teaching platform built to support RFETM: 'We have built a virtual simulation experimental teaching platform, which included the preparation of RA animal models, RT-qPCR and Western blot detection of the effects of drugs on RA pathological indicators' and other modules, 'to help students self-study before RFETM teaching'. Table 4 lists the platform, online theory and technique self-learning, online operation demonstration, and video feedback as available under RFETM and not available under TETM.
requirements: Hosts modules such as preparation of RA animal models and RT-qPCR and Western blot detection so students can self-study experimental theory and techniques
constraints: Intended for self-study before RFETM teaching rather than replacing the in-class experimental projects
examples: The platform's modules mirror mandatory projects, including RA animal model preparation and drug-effect detection on RA pathological indicators.

BMC Medical Education 25:961. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07538-4
title: RFETM research project cycle: small groups design, get teacher review, run, and report on exploratory experiments
description: The RFETM implementation cycle organizes each project so that 'The students were divided into groups, each group consisted of 4 students'; students consult literature on the research background, then 'Under the guidance of the experimental guidance teachers, students designed technical routes and implementation plans, completed feasibility assessments, and developed specific experimental steps.' Teachers review the design's rationality and safety before students conduct the experiments, analyze results and problems, and write experimental reports with teacher inspiration and guidance.
requirements: Groups of four students and experimental guidance teachers who review and evaluate the rationality of the experimental design and the safety of the experiment
target_learners: medical undergraduate students in groups of four
target_learning_goals: experimental design and technical route planning
examples: After completing the experimental projects, students analyzed the experimental results and existing problems and wrote experimental reports, with teachers providing necessary inspiration and guidance.

article_title: Educational improvement through machine learning: Strategic models for better PISA scores.
citation: Alkan Bilal Baris, Kuzucuk Serafettin, Odabasi Şevki Yetkin, Karakuş Leyla. (2025). Educational improvement through machine learning: Strategic models for better PISA scores. PLOS One 20(7): e0326121. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0326121
title: Random Forest Algorithm with Boruta feature selection as a method for identifying important predictors of educational outcomes
description: The article employs the Random Forest Algorithm (RFA) via the Boruta package in R as its analytical framework. Boruta is described as "a wrapping method based on Random Forest and calculates the significance levels of the variables using Z-scores", creating a shadow copy of each variable and retaining only variables with unique information value. The authors argue RFA suits educational data because it handles high-dimensional categorical data, minimises multicollinearity, and captures nonlinear interactions and interactions that classical statistical models miss. Its role in the study is both prediction and evidence-based prioritisation of influential variables for policy makers.
requirements: Categorical pre-processed predictor variables and a binary high/low-performing class variable derived from OECD-average score thresholds
constraints: The authors state the analysis covers only 37 OECD member countries, limiting generalisation beyond the OECD, and that only student-level variables were included, excluding teacher, school and system level variables
RFA does not directly show causal relationships, only predictive power between variables
target_learning_goals: Classifying and predicting country-level PISA performance in reading, mathematics and science
examples: Applied to 24 categorical PISA 2018 variables for 37 OECD countries, producing domain-specific variable rankings and three threshold-based prediction models
key_sources: Alkan Bilal Baris, Kuzucuk Serafettin, Odabasi Şevki Yetkin, Karakuş Leyla. (2025). Educational improvement through machine learning: Strategic models for better PISA scores. PLOS One 20(7): e0326121. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0326121
